definition: A patch lies closer to A when exposed brown or tan soil occupies less of its area and leafy vegetation or open water occupies more. B is dominated by bare or sparsely vegetated agricultural fields.
cues: B has extensive brown–tan fields in true color, appearing cyan or muted gray-green in false color.
A generally has more green vegetation that becomes vivid red in false color.
B shows repeated narrow agricultural strips, with green or red vegetation confined to scattered strips and margins.
Continuous tree cover or open water favors A; water appears blue-green in true color and dark blue in false color.
